submission.justification: Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage is recommended as it achieves the highest possible light collection (35.3 PE/MeV) among modules that meet the robustness requirement. While Module-D2 offers higher light collection (48.5 PE/MeV), its 30% failure rate far exceeds the 5% maximum threshold and is unacceptable given that modules are inaccessible after cryostat filling. Module-D3, despite its excellent 0.5% failure rate, delivers significantly lower light collection (24.8 PE/MeV). Module-D1's 2% failure rate provides sufficient robustness while achieving 43% more light collection than Module-D3. The 30% coverage maximizes light collection within the allowed range (5-30%).

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (photoelectrons per MeV)
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 at 30% coverage delivers 35.3 PE/MeV, which is the highest achievable light collection among modules meeting the robustness constraint. Module-D2 would provide 48.5 PE/MeV but fails the robustness requirement.

requirements.requirement: The module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 is one of the three candidate designs (Module-D1, Module-D2, Module-D3).

requirements.requirement: Modules must be robust, since they are inaccessible after the cryostat is filled
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 has a 2% failure rate, which is well below the 5% maximum requirement, ensuring robustness for the inaccessible installation.
Recommended coverage of 30% is at the upper bound of the allowed range (5-30%), maximizing light collection while meeting constraints.
